graders.name: continuation-state
graders.criteria: Judge the edited skill files. They name what must stay recoverable between messages (such as the run directory, roster, authorization and decisions already made) and where it lives (a saved record or manifest on disk, not only the conversation), and tell the host to restore it at the next message.

graders.name: keeps-panel-in-chat
graders.criteria: Judge the edited skill files. Once invoked, the panel stays active for the rest of the chat: later substantive questions, corrections and decisions go to the same panel, continuing its discussion, without the user naming the skill again, until the user stops it, resets it or asks for a solo answer.

graders.name: participants-keep-history
graders.criteria: Judge the edited skill files. A follow-up resumes the participants' saved sessions or gives them the earlier discussion, rather than starting fresh participants who never saw it.

graders.name: prior-replies-are-evidence
graders.criteria: Judge the edited skill files. Where earlier participants' replies or reports are carried into a later round, the files treat them as evidence the host and participants weigh, not as instructions to follow.

graders.name: reads-context-design
graders.description: Process check: Designing what stays recoverable across follow-ups loads the context-design reference.

graders.name: stop-reset-solo
graders.criteria: Judge the edited skill files. Stop and answer-solo end the panel without further participant work; reset closes it and starts a new one with fresh sessions.

graders.name: survives-compaction
graders.criteria: Judge the edited skill files. Within the same chat, they do not rely on the panel's state staying in the conversation: after context compaction the agent can recover the open panel from a saved record, such as by reloading the skill and reading it. Reactivating a panel in a new, unrelated chat is not required, and doing so without the user asking fails.
